terms.meaning: code that runs in the visitor's browser rather than on the server

sections.name: File setup, ExpectedFile
sections.title: Setup and expected file shape
sections.what: Marks the file as browser code, imports the state helper, and defines what one expected file entry looks like: a name and a description.
sections.why: Each expected persona file needs a name and a note on what it is for.
sections.watch_out: Because this runs in the browser, it can only use data passed to it from the server.

sections.name: PersonaBrowser (part 1)
sections.title: Opening and reading a persona file
sections.what: Toggles a persona file open or closed when its row is clicked and fetches the file text from the persona API when opening. It also defines a download helper that saves the text as a markdown file.
sections.why: Lets the user read persona files on the page without leaving it.
sections.watch_out: If two files are opened quickly, a late response can overwrite the text of the file currently shown.

sections.name: PersonaBrowser (part 2)
sections.title: Core persona file list
sections.what: Lists the expected core files, marking each READY if it exists on the server or PENDING if not. Only READY files can be opened.
sections.why: Shows which files are still missing so the user knows what to add.
sections.watch_out: Readiness is judged only by the file name, so an empty file still shows READY.

sections.name: PersonaBrowser (part 3)
sections.title: Read-only note and resume archive
sections.what: Shows a note that persona files are read-only in production and must be edited in the repo and redeployed. It also lists the resume files found and a count of them.
sections.why: Explains why the page cannot save edits and shows how many resume versions exist.
sections.watch_out: The note says changes only appear after a redeploy, so a new file added to the folder will not show until then.

summary: Browser-side component for viewing persona files. Only its setup was visible.
purpose: Likely lets the user look through the persona files that the persona page loads.
why: Likely reason: the viewer needs interactive controls, so it runs in the browser.
how: Only the setup is visible: it is marked as browser code, imports the state helper, and defines a file entry with a name and a description. The rest is not visible.
inputs: Likely the list of files passed in from the persona page.
risks: Unknown, because most of the file is not visible.
debug: If the list is empty, check the data the persona page passes in. If controls do not respond, check the browser's error console.
